title: A derived-complete module with finite residue over a complete Noetherian ring is finite
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and assume that the canonical map $A\to\widehat A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $M$ be an $A$-module which is derived complete with respect to $I$, meaning that $M[0]$ is derived $I$-complete in $D(A)$ [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]. If $M/IM$ is a finitely generated $A/I$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], then $M$ is a finitely generated $A$-module. Moreover the canonical map $M\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}M/I^nM$ is an isomorphism; this inverse limit consists of compatible sequences of residue classes, with componentwise operations.

source.place: Tag 09BA, lemma-derived-complete-finite, specialized to an I-adically complete ring A

proof.text: First make the multiplication-tower condition concrete. Products of $A$-modules are exact: kernels and images are checked coordinatewise, and a tuple of elements in images has a tuple of preimages by choice. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], products in $D(A)$ are termwise products and multiplication-tower derived limits exist. For any module $L$ and $f\in A$, [def-weil-derived-limit] gives a triangle $T\to(\prod_{n\geq1}L)[0]\xrightarrow{\Delta_f}(\prod_{n\geq1}L)[0]\to T[1]$, where $\Delta_f((a_n))=(a_n-fa_{n+1})$. By [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], $H^0(T)=\ker\Delta_f$, $H^1(T)=\operatorname{coker}\Delta_f$, and all other cohomology vanishes. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], applied to $0\to T$, $T=0$ exactly when $\Delta_f$ is bijective. Thus [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex] says that $L$ is derived $I$-complete exactly when $\Delta_f$ is bijective for every $f\in I$. In particular, in a derived-complete module there is no nonzero sequence $(a_n)$ with $a_n=fa_{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 09BA, lemma-derived-complete-finite, use of derived completeness; multiplication-tower computation underlying Tag 091P, lemma-hom-from-Af

proof.text: We will use cokernel closure, proved directly from step 1. Let $u:L\to N$ be an $A$-linear map between derived $I$-complete modules, put $P=\prod_{n\geq1}L$, $Q=\prod_{n\geq1}N$, and let $U:P\to Q$ act coordinatewise by $u$. For each $f\in I$, the bijections $\Delta_{f,L}$ and $\Delta_{f,N}$ satisfy $\Delta_{f,N}U=U\Delta_{f,L}$, hence also $\Delta_{f,N}^{-1}U=U\Delta_{f,L}^{-1}$. Therefore both $\Delta_{f,N}$ and its inverse preserve $U(P)$ and induce inverse maps on $Q/U(P)\cong\prod_{n\geq1}(N/u(L))$; this canonical identification follows by coordinatewise lifting of quotient classes and the coordinatewise kernel calculation. The induced map is $\Delta_{f,N/u(L)}$, so step 1 proves that $N/u(L)$ is derived $I$-complete.

source.place: Tag 091U, lemma-serre-subcategory, cokernel assertion of part (1), here verified directly using the multiplication-tower criterion of step 1

proof.text: For every finite integer $t\geq0$, put $F=A^t$ with coordinatewise operations. It is ordinarily complete and separated: the canonical map $F\to\varprojlim_kF/I^kF$ is the product of $t$ copies of the assumed isomorphism $A\to\varprojlim_kA/I^k$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Fix $f\in I$. For a sequence $(b_n)$ in $F$, define $a_n\in F$ by the compatible residues $a_n\bmod I^kF=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}f^jb_{n+j}\bmod I^kF$; compatibility holds since the added summand lies in $I^kF$. The equation $a_n-fa_{n+1}=b_n$ holds modulo every $I^kF$ and hence in $F$. Conversely $a_n=fa_{n+1}$ implies $a_n=f^ka_{n+k}\in I^kF$ for every $k$, so $a_n=0$. Therefore $\Delta_f$ is bijective and step 1 proves that $F$ is derived $I$-complete. This also covers $t=0$.

source.place: Tag 09BA, lemma-derived-complete-finite, finite free source over a complete ring; explicit geometric-series verification of Tag 091R, lemma-complete-derived-complete

proof.text: Choose $x_1,\ldots,x_t\in M$ whose residue classes generate $M/IM$, using the hypothesis and [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Define $q:F=A^t\to M$ by $q(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\sum_j a_jx_j$ and put $C=M/q(F)$. The source is derived complete by step 3 and the target by hypothesis; hence the cokernel argument of step 2 makes $C$ derived $I$-complete. For every $m\in M$ the residue-generation assumption gives $m=\sum_j a_jx_j+z$ with $z\in IM$ (lift the residue coefficients to $A$). Consequently every class in $C$ lies in $IC$, so $C/IC=0$.

source.place: Tag 09BA, lemma-derived-complete-finite, choice of residue generators and the cokernel of q

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $I$, allowing $r=0$ when $I=0$. Define $C_0=C$ and $C_j=C/(f_1,\ldots,f_j)C$ for $1\leq j\leq r$. Each $C_j$ is the cokernel of multiplication by $f_j$ on $C_{j-1}$, so induction using step 2 proves that every $C_j$ is derived $I$-complete. The equality $C=IC$ of step 4 gives $C_r=0$.

source.place: Tag 09B9, lemma-derived-complete-zero, proof by successive quotients; used in Tag 09BA

proof.text: Prove $C_j=0$ by descending induction from $j=r$ to $j=0$. If $C_j=0$ and $j\geq1$, then $C_{j-1}/f_jC_{j-1}=0$, so multiplication by $f_j$ on $C_{j-1}$ is surjective. If $a_1\neq0$ were in $C_{j-1}$, recursively choose $a_{n+1}$ with $f_ja_{n+1}=a_n$; this gives a nonzero element of $\ker\Delta_{f_j}$, contradicting step 1 since $C_{j-1}$ is derived complete and $f_j\in I$. Hence $C_{j-1}=0$. Thus $C=0$, including the case $r=0$, where the initial equality $C_r=0$ already says this. The map $q$ is surjective, so the chosen $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ generate $M$ over $A$ by [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Tag 09B9, lemma-derived-complete-zero, compatible-sequence contradiction, completing the finite-generation argument of Tag 09BA

proof.text: The ring $A$ is Noetherian by hypothesis and is $I$-adically complete in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], since this is exactly the canonical-map assumption. Step 6 proves that $M$ is finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] with $(R,J,N)=(A,I,M)$. Its conclusion is precisely that $M\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}M/I^nM$, $m\mapsto(m\bmod I^nM)_n$, is bijective. This is an $A$-linear map to compatible sequences with coordinatewise operations, so its bijectivity is the asserted module isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09BA, lemma-derived-complete-finite, final completeness conclusion; existing finite-module completion theorem
